item.title: Journalists flag Samoa’s draft media protocol
item.description: “It seems that the government is shutting down all avenues to remain transparent. Why does a government do that when there is nothing to hide?”

item.title: Where myth turns to form and fragility to power: An interview with Turkish artist Melis Buyruk
item.description: “Porcelain lives in our collective memory — we grow up with it in our homes and daily rituals — so it already carries meaning before I touch it.”

item.title: When valid visas mean nothing: The Bangladeshi passport crisis at immigration counters
item.description: Thousands of Bangladeshi travellers face a harsh reality as valid visa holders, carrying proper documents, are turned away at airports amid distrust, past violations, and tighter scrutiny by border authorities.

item.title: The honeybee that stung Jamaica and yielded sweetness
item.description: The name “Melissa” is of Greek origin and translates to “honeybee” in English, but [the] fallout felt personal, as if we troubled the hive and threatened the queen.

item.title: Homebound: A Return Home, and to the Ghosts We Carry
item.description: Homebound unravels a heartbreaking story of two friends navigating caste, faith, poverty, and fractured dreams, exposing how modern India’s promises fail those trapped in generational hardship, quiet discrimination, and survival.

item.title: Are ‘hyper-meritocracy’ and feminist backlash driving South Korean young men to the right?
item.description: One interviewee said anonymous online forums have fostered a culture in which blatant misogynistic, racist and sexist jokes and comments are normalized.

item.title: Pakistan seeks justice for environmental harm through climate litigation
item.description: As climate disasters intensify, Pakistan’s courts face growing pressure to deliver environmental justice, even as limited resources, slow proceedings, and shrinking civil society support constrain meaningful legal remedies.

item.title: A voice for the unheard in Myanmar: From the Rakhine coast to the frontlines of truth
item.description: "We decided to present the resilience of female journalists across Myanmar who are working in war-torn areas, rather than focusing solely on our own story."

item.title: Thais and Cambodians speak out against the looming war
item.description: Peace advocates said the war has done nothing for the Thais and Cambodians who have lived together for generations along the 800 km border

item.title: When children disclose abuse, families in rural Andhra Pradesh, India, often respond with silence
item.description: What happens after a child discloses an abuse is determined not only by law, but by the social worlds families must navigate once silence is broken.
